- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 10–20% for the day after a spike.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.50), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply “mean reversion bias” — forecast should be closer to 10–15-day moving average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average.  
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model often misses the “rebound overshoot”; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.25) over 5+ days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 5–10% for next 5–7 days.
